title: Adsorption of Pb (II) and Zn (II) ions from aqueous solutions by Red Earth
author: Esmaeili, Eslami

steps.title: Crush and sieve Red Earth
steps.instruction: Crush the local natural Red Earth (RE) using a jaw crusher, then sieve the material and collect particles that pass through a 50‑mesh screen.

steps.title: Dry the adsorbent
steps.instruction: Spread the sieved RE in a thin layer and allow it to dry at laboratory temperature for two weeks.

steps.title: Record chemical composition
steps.instruction: Analyze the dried RE by X‑ray fluorescence (XRF, Philips PW1730, Netherlands) and record the weight percentages: SiO₂ 58.0 %, Al₂O₃ 15.2 %, Fe₂O₃ 3.1 %, CaO 4.7 %, MgO 0.8 %, Na₂O (trace), K₂O 0.1 %, loss on ignition (LOI) 10.7 %.

steps.title: Prepare metal stock solutions
steps.instruction: Using analytical‑grade nitrate salts (≥99 % purity, Merck), dissolve the salts in deionized water to make 1000 mg L⁻¹ stock solutions of Pb(II) and Zn(II). Store each stock in a tightly sealed bottle.

steps.title: Prepare working solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the appropriate volume of the 1000 mg L⁻¹ stock with deionized water to obtain the desired initial metal concentrations for the batch tests.

steps.title: Adjust solution pH
steps.instruction: Measure the pH of each working solution with a YSI portable meter (HQ 40d, Hach, Germany) and adjust to the required value using 1.0 N NaOH or 1.0 N HNO₃.

steps.title: Set up batch adsorption experiment
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL batch container, add the measured volume (50 mL) of metal solution and a known mass of the dried RE (particle size 50 mesh). Maintain the mixture at 27 ± 1 °C and shake at 150 rpm for the predetermined contact time.

steps.title: Measure equilibrium metal concentration
steps.instruction: After shaking, separate the RE (e.g., by filtration or centrifugation) and determine the residual Pb(II) or Zn(II) concentration in the supernatant using atomic absorption spectroscopy (Varian AA‑975 or AA‑1275).

steps.title: Calculate removal percentage
steps.instruction: Compute the percentage removal of metal ions using %RE = ((C₀ – Cₑ) / C₀) × 100, where C₀ is the initial concentration and Cₑ is the equilibrium concentration (mg L⁻¹).

steps.title: Calculate adsorption capacity
steps.instruction: Calculate the adsorption capacity qₑ (mg g⁻¹) with qₑ = ((C₀ – Cₑ) × V) / m, where V is the solution volume (L) and m is the mass of RE (g).
